periods.analysis: The Procurement Modernization Project opens this reporting arc at 21% complete and green, with quarter-over-quarter movement not yet established for this series. The e-procurement platform is live and complete, and the vendor self-service portal is complete, giving us a controlled foundation for requisitions, approvals, and vendor data maintenance. P-card policy rollout remains in progress with a 20-day due offset, while the cycle-time target review is not started with a 100-day due offset, so the principal control risk is policy adoption getting ahead of measurement discipline. Early production checks in the Munis-to-BidBridge interface show clean purchase-order routing for Finance, Public Works, and Parks, but I want exception logs reviewed before we widen the aperture.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by keeping daily exception review on the AP-PO match queue and publishing a short weekly control report through the Finance PMO. Extend the vendor portal by onboarding the first 75 high-volume vendors in commodities 910, 918, and 968, with W-9 validation and banking-change controls verified before activation. Keep the P-card rollout gated until department liaisons complete policy attestation and merchant-category-code blocks are tested.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 21% to 28%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7 percentage points, and the project remains green. The completed e-procurement platform and completed vendor self-service portal are now handling routine intake for coastal maintenance, facilities, and IT purchases without material control exceptions. P-card policy rollout is still in progress with a 20-day due offset, and the cycle-time target review remains not started with a 100-day due offset, which is acceptable only if we keep the interim baseline intact. The most useful signal this quarter is that buyer queue aging in the Central Purchasing team is visible by department, which gives us a better early-warning system than email follow-up ever did.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the 7-point pace by assigning each buyer a weekly queue clean-up target and having the Purchasing Manager certify aged requisitions over 10 business days. Extend the portal rollout to construction and professional-services vendors, but require dual approval on bank-account edits and retain the audit trail in the vendor master file. Prepare the P-card policy for final departmental review by testing three live scenarios: emergency repair, conference travel, and recurring software subscription.

periods.analysis: The project advanced from 28% to 35%, another 7 percentage-point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green. The live e-procurement platform and completed vendor portal are stable through the heavier winter invoice period, including storm-drain materials, fleet parts, and public-safety supplies. P-card policy rollout remains in progress with a 20-day due offset, while the cycle-time target review remains not started with a 100-day due offset; that sequence is manageable, but it should not drift into informal practice. We now have enough transaction history from requisition groups FIN-01 through PW-06 to see where approvals are slowing, and no single department is presenting an uncontained risk.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by locking the current workflow configuration for one full close cycle and documenting any override approved by Finance Administration. Extend training to the next cohort of 40 cardholders and approvers, using the actual Harborview travel, small-tools, and emergency-purchase cases rather than generic examples. Begin assembling the cycle-time data dictionary now so the later target review starts from controlled definitions rather than anecdote.

periods.analysis: Completion increased from 35% to 42%, a 7 percentage-point quarter-over-quarter movement, and status remains green. The completed platform and vendor portal continue to support a cleaner procure-to-pay path, particularly for summer parks programming, marina maintenance, and street resurfacing purchase orders. The P-card policy rollout is still in progress with a 20-day due offset, and the cycle-time target review is still not started with a 100-day due offset, so my focus is on preventing shadow procedures from forming while the formal policy is being finalized. Controls testing on split-purchase detection and inactive-vendor holds produced useful exceptions, but nothing that threatens the project schedule.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green result by running monthly split-purchase analytics against P-card and purchase-order activity, with exception sign-off by department directors. Extend self-service vendor onboarding to seasonal recreation and right-of-way contractors, but require insurance and business-license fields to be completed before any solicitation response is accepted. Set a firm readiness checklist for the cycle-time target review, including requisition start time, buyer assignment time, approval completion, and PO issue time.

periods.analysis: The project moved from 42% to 49%, again a 7 percentage-point quarter-over-quarter increase, and remains green. We are now past the midpoint of practical adoption even though reported completion is 49%, because the completed e-procurement platform and completed vendor portal are embedded in daily purchasing behavior. P-card policy rollout remains in progress with a 20-day due offset, and cycle-time target review remains not started with a 100-day due offset; the watch item is whether departments treat draft policy language as final without completing attestations. Harborview’s growth is showing up in higher solicitation volume for traffic signal work and facility improvements, and the new routing table is giving us the control visibility needed for that volume.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the trajectory by refreshing approval delegations for all departments before the fall capital-procurement push and removing users who changed roles during the summer. Extend adoption by converting the top 25 recurring blanket purchase orders to catalog-style ordering with pre-approved pricing and budget checks. Require P-card attestation completion before any card limit increases are approved for the new fiscal operating cycle.

periods.analysis: Completion rose from 49% to 56%, a 7 percentage-point quarter-over-quarter improvement, and the project remains green. The completed e-procurement platform and vendor self-service portal are now supporting year-end purchasing controls, including encumbrance checks and vendor-master clean-up before close. The P-card policy rollout remains in progress with a 20-day due offset, while cycle-time target review remains not started with a 100-day due offset; that is still within a controlled posture, but the window for informal metrics is closing. The strongest operational gain this quarter is that AP can now match invoices for facilities contracts HV-FAC-24-11 and fleet parts blanket PO BP-4427 without manual email reconstruction.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the green status by using the year-end close to reconcile open purchase orders, inactive vendors, and unmatched receipts in one controlled workplan. Extend the modernization effort to contract administrators by training them on receipt entry, amendment routing, and retainage documentation in the platform. Schedule the cycle-time target review kickoff now, but do not publish targets until the data definitions and exception rules are approved by Finance.

periods.analysis: The project advanced from 56% to 63%, another 7 percentage-point quarter-over-quarter increase, and remains green. With the e-procurement platform and vendor portal complete, the work has shifted from installation risk to operating discipline across departments. P-card policy rollout is still in progress with a 20-day due offset, and cycle-time target review is still not started with a 100-day due offset; the project is healthy, but those two items now carry more schedule significance than they did a year ago. Audit sampling of Harborview Transit parts purchases, Library materials orders, and IT software renewals shows consistent approval evidence, which is exactly the control record we need for an AA-rated city.
periods.recommendations: Sustain progress by adding procurement-control checkpoints to the quarterly internal audit plan, with samples drawn from P-card, purchase order, and vendor-master transactions. Extend the vendor portal to include automated reminders for expiring insurance and certifications, starting with construction, janitorial, and marine-services vendors. Convert the P-card rollout from general training to targeted remediation for departments with late reconciliations or repeated coding corrections.

periods.analysis: Completion increased from 63% to 70%, a 7 percentage-point quarter-over-quarter movement, and the project remains green. The chronological pattern is steady: completed platform, completed vendor portal, disciplined adoption, and no material control failure as Harborview’s purchasing volume grows. P-card policy rollout remains in progress with a 20-day due offset, and cycle-time target review remains not started with a 100-day due offset, so the next phase must convert stable operations into measurable performance standards. The project is in a strong position, but I would not call it finished until policy closure, target setting, and management reporting are working together.
periods.recommendations: Preserve the green status by setting a 90-day closeout plan for the P-card policy, including final legal review, department attestation, cardholder certification, and post-implementation testing. Extend the modernization gains by launching a procurement performance dashboard that reports requisition-to-PO cycle time, vendor onboarding time, exception rates, and P-card reconciliation timeliness by department. Prepare the cycle-time target review with a controlled baseline from the last two closed quarters and require Finance approval before targets are used for public scorecard reporting.

periods.analysis: 90% complete. 3 of 4 milestones are done. Next up: Cycle-time target review (due Nov 3, 2026).
periods.recommendations: No action needed. Continue on the current plan.
